date.source: Posted to Isamu League's own IL Events sub-forum; no in-story date is given in the broadcast text itself, so the date follows the thread's own posting date.

matches.note: Randall Beetwix won the first match in Isamu League's history by pinfall with the Prophetic Finale (a double-underhook DDT); he twisted his ankle stepping through the ropes on his way out afterward.

An impromptu, unscheduled match: colour commentator Nate Narwin, filling time after Naoki Inoue's own scheduled opponent no-showed, broke from the announce table and attacked Inoue with a whiskey bottle, then pinned him following his own Intoxicated Rage (a vertical piledriver through the ringside table) and a chair shot. Referee Nori Tanaka called it as an official, ranking-points-counting match.
Jonathan Marx submitted Riddick with Marxism (STF) in the main event of Isamu League's first broadcast; Riddick, returning to the ring for the first time since 2008, could not answer the hold.

appearances.note: Billed against Naoki Inoue; arrested in a bar-area brawl before the match and never appeared.
Started the bar-area brawl during the opening match that led to his own arrest.
Billed against Jun Nakagawa; the match never happened after a backstage confrontation turned into a real fight.
Fought Jun Nakagawa backstage in the medical room, wrecking it and cancelling their own scheduled match.
Billed against Masaharu Keichigawa; the match never happened after a backstage confrontation turned into a real fight.
Fought Masaharu Keichigawa backstage in the medical room, wrecking it and cancelling their own scheduled match.
Assaulted by Riddick after the main event, blinded with powder and driven through a table with the Paralyzer (a Russian neck drop) off the ring apron.
Assaulted Jonathan Marx after losing the main event.
Opened the broadcast with an in-character monologue on his own promotion's founding.

date.source: Posted to Isamu League's own IL Events sub-forum; no in-story date is given in the broadcast text itself, so the date follows the thread's own posting date.

matches.note: Reached its own twenty-minute time limit and was ruled a draw, the show's only scheduled match.

appearances.note: Hit Riddick with I Heart Head Trauma (a top-rope splash) off the top rope, driving him through a barbed-wire table Riddick had set on fire, after the match.
Attacked goldFISH with brass knuckles after the match, then set a barbed-wire table on fire, before goldFISH turned the table on him.
Announced Isamu League's own first pay-per-view, National Threat I, and a one-night tournament to crown the fed's first Tsunawoharu Champion.

name: Lessons In Bloodshed: Lesson 3

date.source: No show-thread was ever completed for this show; this date is when it was first announced to come out, in the fed's own news article of 28 March 2010 announcing the card (Jonathan Marx v. Randall Beetwix; goldFISH v. Nate Narwin).

notes: Repeatedly postponed in the fed's own scheduling thread (28 March - 25 April 2010, blamed on both co-writers' real-life commitments, with a target of "the week of May 10") and never released; no later document in the held record mentions it again before the fed's own 15 July 2010 hiatus announcement.

name: National Threat I

date.source: Announced by IL Promoter Joey Clerk on the Lesson 2 broadcast (23 March 2010) as the fed's own first pay-per-view and the site of a one-night tournament, open to the whole roster, to crown the first Tsunawoharu Champion; no month-specific date was ever given beyond "June."

notes: No card, bracket, or further mention survives anywhere in the held record; the fed's own hiatus announcement (15 July 2010) confirms nothing past Lesson 2 was ever produced.
